text:
Mike (sales): Hey team — running a POC with Acme and they're hitting 401s on /v1/generate and intermittent 429s. Using the backend key we handed them from the sales console. Can someone help triage? Org: acme-corp, Project: p-prod

Deploy Bot: rate-limit: tenant=acme-corp key=sk-poc-*** burst_exceeded -> 429 returned

Anna (SE): Can you paste the curl you used and the full response headers/body? 401 usually points to a token org/project binding issue or using a frontend key by mistake.

Mike (sales): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-12345" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Project: p-prod" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{ "error": "invalid_token", "detail": "org mismatch" }
Also sometimes we get HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests with body "rate limit exceeded"

Anna (SE): Hmm. Two quick asks: 1) include the x-rd-request-id from the response headers, 2) run the token introspect to see token bindings:  

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/introspect \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-12345"
```

That will show token_org and token_project. 401 with "org mismatch" means the token's org doesn't match the request org header or the tenant the endpoint expects.

Sam (eng-oncall): Throwing this into logs now, send me the x-rd-request-id and I'll grep.

Mike (sales): x-rd-request-id: rd-9f3a2b

Sam (eng-oncall): Log snippet for rd-9f3a2b -> auth_check failed: token_project=p-prod token_org=acme-corp request_org=acme-prod reason=ORGANIZATION_MISMATCH
Also saw 14 retry attempts from their client in 30s which bumped them into the unknown-token throttle -> observed 429s as a defensive measure.

Anna (SE): So root cause: token is bound to acme-corp but the request is being routed with org header acme-prod (looks like a naming mismatch between their env values). Options: 
- Use a token scoped to acme-prod (generate a project-scoped key under Projects > p-prod in the Console) OR
- Ensure the request uses the correct org header (X-Org: acme-corp) or remove X-Project if using an org-scoped key.

Elaine (SRE): Note for the customer: repeated failed auth attempts count toward a protective burst limit for unknown tokens. We temporarily throttle unknown/invalid tokens (default: 50/min burst) to reduce abuse. Recommend pausing automated retries while you rotate keys so you don't get a secondary 429. Also ensure keys are never embedded in client-side code.

Mike (sales): Customer wants a one-liner they can run to check the token binding and then get an immediate project key if needed. Also asked whether switching to a project key affects billing.

Anna (SE): One-liner to introspect token (shows token_org/token_project):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/introspect -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>"
```

To create a project-scoped key: go to Console -> Projects -> p-prod -> Create API key (or have me create temp key). Billing: unchanged — keys don't change billing entity; usage is billed to the tenant/account associated with the project.

Mike (sales): Got it. I'll ask them to pause retries, run the introspect, and either rotate to a project key or correct the org header. For follow-up: if they still see 401 after rotating, we'll hand off to eng for a deeper look.

Anna (SE): Also leaving this: if you need a quick temp key I can create one scoped to p-prod and post it in the secure channel. :thumbsup:

Mike (sales): Thanks all — sending to customer now. Will update thread. Closing the swarm unless we get another error back within 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
